notes: Arturia Buchla Easel V emulates the Buchla Music Easel, a self-contained 'west coast' synthesis system designed by Don Buchla in the early 1970s. Unlike Moog-style east coast synthesis, the Easel uses a Complex Oscillator (combining a modulating and carrier oscillator) and a Lowpass Gate (combining VCA and filter in one element) for a fundamentally different timbral character ΓÇö sounds bloom, breathe, and shimmer rather than cut and punch. The modulation index controls how deeply the modulation oscillator distorts the carrier, producing anything from subtle FM shimmer to complex clangorous spectra. This instrument is best suited to experimental music, generative compositions, drone textures, and cinematic sound design.

Expression.description: Lowpass Gate level ΓÇö the primary dynamic control, opening the combined VCA/filter gate

Modulation.description: Modulation index ΓÇö depth of FM modulation from the modulating oscillator into the carrier

Portamento Time.description: Portamento time ΓÇö glide between pitches

Complex Osc Timbre.description: Complex oscillator timbre/waveform morph ΓÇö shifts harmonic content of the carrier oscillator

Modulation Index.description: FM modulation index depth ΓÇö higher values create more complex, inharmonic spectra

Lowpass Gate Level.description: Lowpass Gate level offset ΓÇö sets the baseline opening of the combined gate/filter

Mod Osc Rate.description: Modulation oscillator rate ΓÇö from sub-audio to audio rate, crossing into FM territory

Mod Osc Depth.description: Modulation oscillator depth applied to carrier pitch ΓÇö vibrato at low rates, FM at audio rates

Attack.description: Envelope attack time ΓÇö the Easel's envelope shapes the Lowpass Gate opening

Decay.description: Envelope decay/release time ΓÇö controls how the Lowpass Gate closes after a note

Reverb.description: Reverb send level ΓÇö adds space and depth to the Easel's organic tones
